Apple system Guided Access vs your app's kiosk marketing — listing honesty

Apple ships Guided Access in iOS Settings → Accessibility. It locks the device to one app until a passcode ends the session and can disable hardware buttons during the session. Third-party apps often market "works in Guided Access", kiosk mode, lock-to-this-app, classroom single-app use, or retail display lock. AppLocale rewrites listing copy from what your US page already claims:

Kiosk-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Single-app lock marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe kiosk and classroom lock — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Guided Access vs generic kiosk lock

US pages use "Guided Access", "Single App Mode", "Lock to one app", or "Kiosk mode." China storefront copy often uses 引导式访问 when referencing Apple's Accessibility feature, 单一应用锁定 for session lock UX, or 柜台模式 / 自助终端 for retail POS — depending on whether you mean system Guided Access compatibility, in-app lock sessions, or enterprise display use. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual lock scope.

Session passcode vs parental PIN

Screenshot galleries often label exit flows: session passcode (会话密码 / 退出密码), teacher unlock, or cashier exit. These signal exam proctoring and retail kiosk intent — different from Screen Time passcodes that gate daily usage limits. Match the exit model your English listing and screenshots actually show.

Classroom, exam, POS, and museum contexts

Each vertical uses distinct buyer vocabulary: 课堂锁定应用 for classroom tablets, 考试模式 for exam proctoring, 柜台模式 for retail POS, 展厅模式 for museum displays. Generic "kiosk" alone may miss China Search intent for your actual buyer segment.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need lock-session search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 引导式访问, 单一应用锁定, and 课堂锁定 each signal different intent from generic parental-control keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Lock to one app" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Why machine-translated kiosk copy fails

  • Literal "Single App Mode" → awkward 单一应用模式 as a product subtitle instead of commerce-idiomatic 单一应用锁定
  • Generic "Kiosk mode" → 自助服务机 (hardware kiosk sense) instead of 柜台模式 (retail session-lock sense buyers expect)
  • English badge headlines preserved on zh-Hans screenshots — "Lock to one app" with no Chinese benefit line beside it
  • Overlay text overflow — long English Guided Access captions pasted into short screenshot callout zones truncate on device
  • Conflating 引导式访问 with Screen Time parental controls — buyers searching for exam lock or POS kiosk may not match usage-limit keywords
  • Inconsistent vocabulary between listing description, promotional text, and screenshot captions when all three mention kiosk lock

Machine translation is fine for internal drafts. Finished kiosk strings need idiomatic zh-Hans that states what single-app lock workflows you ship — while keeping accurate scope. AppLocale rewrites by hand; we do not deliver raw Google Translate or LLM output as finished copy.
